answers.question: multiple-chat
answers.answer: Because nobody ever reduced AnA to one place. There is one main AnA conversation. It follows you around: it sits in the right-hand panel on most screens and moves to the middle on the “Conversation” screen. The code also runs three other AnA conversations, each with its own memory and none sharing it with the main one: one inside the document editor, one inside the eCTD co-author and one inside risk-based monitoring. Those three start blank every time you come back. On top of that come shortcuts into AnA. Some are links: “Conversation” in the left menu, “Get help” in the top bar, “Ask AnA” in the Cmd-K search and the task tray. Others are typing boxes in the middle of Home, Project home and Template library. The boxes on Home and Project home do not continue the conversation in the right panel. They start a new one and take you to another screen. So most screens show you three to five ways into AnA at once, and on the editor and eCTD co-author screens some of them lead to different conversations. Many buttons elsewhere (“Open in editor”, “Transmit”, “Fix”, “contact sales”) also don't do their job; they type a request to AnA instead. This happened because the July 2026 design kit put AnA beside every screen and also kept a full-page AnA. When the editor and eCTD screens had no room for that column, sessions gave each one its own AnA rather than making one work everywhere. The repository's own design document says “one composer”, meaning one place to type to AnA. Merging them was flagged in September and sent to you for a decision, and the code shows it never happened. The reports count differently: 8 places to type, 4 live conversations (5 counting a fallback used only in tests), or “five AnA hosts” in the 2026-09-24 work. All three counts are correct; they measure different things.

claims.claim: The code makes five separate useAnaChat calls. Each keeps its own transcript and thread in component state, and no store is shared between them. The five are the shell chat, the editor's chat, the eCTD co-author's chat, the RBM dock's chat, and a fallback inside ConversationThread that only tests use.

claims.claim: The editor, eCTD co-author and RBM chats start empty on every visit because none of them passes a thread id. Whether their server threads show up anywhere else was not verified.
claims.evidence: DocumentWorkbench.tsx:1419-1430; EctdCoauthor.tsx:335-343; Rbm.tsx:160-168 (chat-surfaces.md §0, which marks the cross-visibility point 'not verified')
claims.correction: The reason given is imprecise. Passing a thread id would not restore the transcript. useAnaChat.ts:494 only seeds threadIdRef, messages always start as [] (:476), and history loads only through an explicit loadThread call (ConversationThread.tsx:1077). The missing thread id actually means the first send after each mount creates a new server thread. 'Every visit' also needs qualifying: the transcript lasts as long as the component stays mounted, so it empties on each mount, not on each document or tab change. The code also partly answers the 'not verified' point. server/routes/ana-ri/stream.ts:907-914 creates the thread with programIdForThread(project_id). The editor passes programId (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:911, :1421) and eCTD passes window.C2C_PROJECT.id (EctdCoauthor.tsx:214-217, :337). So when a program is open, their threads get chat_threads.program_id. GET /api/chat/threads?program_id= (server/routes/chat/threads.ts:43-63) lists them with no screen filter. That makes them appear in ProjectHome's Conversations list (ProjectHome.tsx:965), from which they can be resumed on the conversation screen. RBM passes `study` (Rbm.tsx:162), which gets a program_id only if it is a program UUID. None of this was checked at runtime.

answers.question: rail-vs-center
answers.answer: The AnA panel on the right of nearly every screen was copied from the July 2026 design kit. That kit drew every screen as three columns: menu, work area, AnA. When the new interface was installed on 2026-07-07, that AnA column came with it onto every screen. A June 2026 internal study had separately asked for AnA in two places, a right-hand panel everywhere plus a full-screen mode, and that is exactly what got built. So the AnA in the middle of the Conversation screen is not a second AnA. It is the same conversation, moved from the right panel into the centre, and the right panel hides on that screen. The panel appears on 117 of 123 screens and is switched off on only 6. It starts collapsed to a thin strip, but the first time you press any “Ask AnA” button it opens. Your browser then remembers that, so it stays open on every screen from then on. Where it really does clash is Home and Project home, which also put a typing box in the middle that starts a new conversation. On the editor, eCTD co-author and monitoring screens the panel was turned off because it didn't fit, and those screens grew their own, different AnA instead. No document ever specified one AnA in one place. The repository's own UI directive actually said the chat belongs in the centre and the right side should be a drawer for files and artifacts, not a chat; the code did the reverse. One correction to the record: your decision of 2026-07-28 to stop the rail being collapsed was about the left-hand navigation menu, not this AnA panel.

answers.question: canvas
answers.answer:
You can have part of it today, in one place only, and the fuller Claude-style version was built and then thrown away. In late June 2026 a “Document Studio” was built with chat on the left, the document on the right, a drag handle between them, and a Download DOCX button. It was merged switched off. The July interface replacement never connected it, and on 2026-08-04 a cleanup session deleted it as unreachable dead code. What exists now was added on 2026-10-01 at your direction. On the Conversation screen only, a document AnA drafts appears as a card inside the chat. You click “Open full editor”, and the real editor opens to the right of the conversation, where you can edit it section by section. Compared with Claude, here is what is missing:
- It never opens by itself.
- You don't see the text being written. The whole draft arrives at once after AnA finishes, and the card refreshes only when her turn ends.
- You can't download a draft as Word or PDF. Export is blocked until a document is frozen or approved, as a Part 11 control. Filing it to the Vault as PDF or Word does work, and whether to allow a working-copy download is your governance call.
- There is no list of everything AnA built.
- There is no draggable divider, and below 1100px the chat disappears.
- AnA can't propose edits into the open document or read its text. You insert her answers by clicking.
- On every other screen there is no canvas at all. The right side there is the AnA panel, and its draft card says “Open in conversation” and moves you to a different screen.
The plain reason: the July kit gave the right side of every screen to the AnA chat, so the only screen with room for a right-hand document is the one where that chat moved to the middle. No current design document asked for a right-hand canvas across the product. Only the deleted Studio did.

answers.question: app-split
answers.answer: Nobody decided that features should be separate apps instead of living inside the client's work. The reports found no such decision anywhere. It happened by inheritance. In July 2026 the whole interface was replaced by a design kit whose registry had one screen per capability, and that registry was copied “verbatim”. One change took the product from 33 to 81 screens; it reached about 118 by mid-August and 121–123 today. Each screen then became a separately priced, separately licensed module, and the launch definition counts the product as “seven apps”. So scope, billing and launch all set hard around those app boundaries. The data got split the same way. Tasks and readiness use a different project ID from the one the project page uses, so your project page literally tells the user “Tasks & submission readiness aren't wired to this workspace yet” and “The document vault opens in its own workspace”. Submission Center makes you choose the program again, and QMS is not linked from any project, document or review screen. When consolidation was proposed, a 2026-09-24 pass kept every screen. It applied rules recorded as yours, including “keep what came from the design kits”. A 2026-09-10 work order asking you to choose the pilot set of screens has no recorded answer. Your “all starts with a project” principle was applied to how records are stored, not to how screens are organised. The repository's own design documents say the opposite of what was built: apps should be “callable capabilities, not standalone kingdoms”. These figures come from reading the code, not from running the app. In production a customer can reach about 41 of 121 screens, and choosing 4 of the 5 main client types lands on a “Not in this release” page.

answers.question: how-we-got-here
answers.answer:
Here is the honest account. This product has been built by many separate AI sessions: 57 touched the AnA files, and 14 of them created or moved a place where you talk to AnA. Each was given one narrow task, and none had the overall screen layout as its job. The direction then changed several times.
- **April 2026.** The rules were explicitly chat-first and Claude-like.
- **June.** A study asked for AnA in two places, a right panel plus a full screen. A Claude-style studio with chat on the left and the document on the right was built and left switched off.
- **July.** The whole interface was swapped, almost mechanically, for a design kit with one screen per capability and an AnA column on every screen. The Claude-like pieces were never connected to it.
- **August.** A cleanup session deleted those Claude-like pieces as dead code.
Since then, the rules sessions work under have kept them polishing what exists instead of simplifying it. They may not add screens until launch is green. They may not delete a screen without naming its replacement; otherwise the deletion is your decision. And a September pass applied a rule recorded as yours, “keep what came from the design kits”. The questions that needed you were written into documents but never answered: which screens the pilot should have, merging AnA's typing boxes, and folding duplicate screens together. When you asked on 2026-09-24 for no duplication and less clutter, this session made AnA's progress display identical in all five places it appears, rather than reducing them to one. When you asked on 2026-10-01 for the canvas to become an editor, it was built, but only on the Conversation screen. So what you see is the sum of many individually reasonable steps with nobody steering the whole. The launch playbook that is supposed to assign the workstreams is not even in the repository. Two limits on this account. The history before 2026-09-03 was read from GitHub, because the local copy is incomplete. And every screen description comes from reading the code; nobody ran the app.
